sanskrit: te yayur bhīmasenasya samīpam amitaujasaḥ yuyudhānaprabhṛtayo mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Then those warriors of boundless might—Yuyudhāna and the rest, together with the two sons of Mādrī—drew near to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: te sametya susaṃrabdhāḥ sahitāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ maheṣvāsavarair guptaṃ droṇānīkaṃ bibhitsavaḥ
english: United and roused to fury, those bulls among men joined forces, eager to break through Droṇa's host, which was guarded by the foremost of great archers.

sanskrit: samāpetur mahāvīryā bhīmaprabhṛtayo rathāḥ tān pratyagṛhṇād avyagro droṇo 'pi rathināṃ varaḥ
english: On rushed those car-warriors of mighty valour, Bhīma at their head; and Droṇa too, the best of chariot-fighters, received them undismayed.

sanskrit: mahābalān atirathān vīrān samaraśobhinaḥ bāhyaṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ kṛtvā tāvakāḥ pāṇḍavān yayuḥ
english: Casting all fear of death aside, your warriors advanced upon those Pāṇḍava heroes—mighty, surpassing car-warriors, splendid in battle.

sanskrit: sādinaḥ sādino 'bhyaghnaṃs tathaiva rathino rathān āsīc chaktyasisaṃpāto yuddham āsīt paraśvadhaiḥ
english: Horseman struck down horseman, and likewise car-warrior smote car-warrior; there was a clashing of lances and swords, and the battle raged with battle-axes.

sanskrit: nikṛṣṭam asiyuddhaṃ ca babhūva kaṭukodayam kuñjarāṇāṃ ca saṃghātair yuddham āsīt sudāruṇam
english: A close and bitter sword-fight broke out, fierce in its issue; and through the colliding masses of elephants the combat grew exceedingly terrible.

sanskrit: apatat kuñjarād anyo hayād anyas tv avākśirāḥ naro bāṇena nirbhinno rathād anyaś ca māriṣa
english: One man fell headlong from an elephant, another from a horse, and another, pierced through by an arrow, dropped from his chariot, O lord.

sanskrit: tatrānyasya ca saṃmarde patitasya vivarmaṇaḥ śiraḥ pradhvaṃsayām āsa vakṣasy ākramya kuñjaraḥ
english: And there, in the crush, an elephant trod upon the breast of another man who had fallen, his armour stripped away, and crushed his head to pieces.

sanskrit: apare 'py aparāñ jaghnur vāraṇāḥ patitān narān viṣāṇaiś cāvaniṃ gatvā vyabhindan rathino bahūn
english: Other elephants slew other men who had fallen, and driving their tusks into the earth, ripped open many a car-warrior.

sanskrit: narāntraiḥ ke cid apare viṣāṇālagnasaṃsravaiḥ babhramuḥ śataśo nāgā mṛdnantaḥ śataśo narān
english: Elephants by the hundred roamed about, their tusks clotted and dripping with men's entrails, trampling men by the hundred.

sanskrit: kāṃsyāyasatanutrāṇān narāśvarathakuñjarān patitān pothayāṃ cakrur dvipāḥ sthūlanaḍān iva
english: The elephants ground down fallen men, horses, chariots, and elephants, clad in armour of bronze and iron, as though they were thick reeds.

sanskrit: gṛdhrapatrādhivāsāṃsi śayanāni narādhipāḥ hrīmantaḥ kālasaṃpakvāḥ suduḥkhāny adhiśerate
english: Proud lords of men, ripened now by Time, lay down in anguish upon their beds—those couches haunted by vultures' wings.

sanskrit: hanti smātra pitā putraṃ rathenābhyativartate putraś ca pitaraṃ mohān nirmaryādam avartata
english: There a father slew his son and drove his chariot over him, and a son in his bewilderment slew his father—all bounds were overthrown.

sanskrit: akṣo bhagno dhvajaś chinnaś chatram urvyāṃ nipātitam yugārdhaṃ chinnam ādāya pradudrāva tathā hayaḥ
english: An axle was shattered, a banner cut down, a parasol flung to the earth; and a horse, dragging half a severed yoke, bolted away.

sanskrit: sāsir bāhur nipatitaḥ śiraś chinnaṃ sakuṇḍalam gajenākṣipya balinā rathaḥ saṃcūrṇitaḥ kṣitau
english: An arm fell, still grasping its sword; a severed head dropped with its earrings; and a mighty elephant, seizing a chariot, dashed it to splinters upon the ground.

sanskrit: rathinā tāḍito nāgo nārācenāpatad vyasuḥ sārohaś cāpatad vājī gajenātāḍito bhṛśam
english: An elephant, struck by a car-warrior's iron shaft, fell down lifeless; and a horse with its rider, smitten hard by an elephant, fell as well.

sanskrit: nirmaryādaṃ mahad yuddham avartata sudāruṇam hā tāta hā putra sakhe kvāsi tiṣṭha kva dhāvasi
english: A great and most terrible battle raged on, with no bounds left: "Alas, father! Alas, my son! Friend, where are you? Stand! Whither do you flee?"

sanskrit: praharāhara jahy enaṃ smitakṣveḍitagarjitaiḥ ity evam uccarantyaḥ sma śrūyante vividhā giraḥ
english: "Strike! Strike! Slay this one!"—with laughter and shouts and roaring, such varied cries were heard ringing forth.

sanskrit: narasyāśvasya nāgasya samasajjata śoṇitam upāśāmyad rajo bhaumaṃ bhīrūn kaśmalam āviśat
english: The blood of man, of horse, and of elephant ran together and mingled; the dust of the earth was laid, and faintness came over the timid.

sanskrit: āsīt keśaparāmarśo muṣṭiyuddhaṃ ca dāruṇam nakhair dantaiś ca śūrāṇam advīpe dvīpam icchatām
english: There was tearing of hair and a savage fight with fists, and combat with nails and teeth among warriors who, weaponless, sought weapons where there were none.

sanskrit: tatrācchidyata vīrasya sakhaḍgo bāhur udyataḥ sadhanuś cāparasyāpi saśaraḥ sāṅkuśas tathā
english: There one hero's upraised arm was severed, sword and all; and another's likewise, holding bow and arrow and goad together.

sanskrit: prākrośad anyam anyo 'tra tathānyo vimukho 'dravat anyaḥ prāptasya cānyasya śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: Here one man shouted at another, while another turned his back and fled; and one struck the head from the body of another who had come within his reach.

sanskrit: śabdam abhyadravac cānyaḥ śabdād anyo 'dravad bhṛśam svān anyo 'tha parān anyo jaghāna niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: One charged toward a sound, while another fled hard away from a sound; one slew his own men, and another the foe, with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: giriśṛṅgopamaś cātra nārācena nipātitaḥ mātaṅgo nyapatad bhūmau nadīrodha ivoṣṇage
english: There an elephant like a mountain-peak, struck down by an iron shaft, fell upon the earth like a riverbank crumbling in the hot season.

sanskrit: tathaiva rathinaṃ nāgaḥ kṣaran girir ivārujat adhyatiṣṭhat padā bhūmau sahāśvaṃ sahasārathim
english: Likewise an elephant, like a streaming mountain, crushed a car-warrior, and pinned him to the ground beneath its foot, together with his horses and his charioteer.

sanskrit: śūrān praharato dṛṣṭvā kṛtāstrān rudhirokṣitān bahūn apy āviśan moho bhīrūn hṛdayadurbalān
english: At the sight of those many warriors, skilled in arms and bathed in blood, smiting on, a stupor seized the timid and faint of heart.

sanskrit: sarvam āvignam abhavan na prājñāyata kiṃ cana sainye ca rajasā dhvaste nirmaryādam avartata
english: All became confusion; nothing could be discerned; and when the army was blotted out by dust, every bound was overthrown.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatiḥ śīghram ayaṃ kāla iti bruvan nityābhitvaritān eva tvarayām āsa pāṇḍavān
english: Then the commander, crying swiftly "Now is the hour!", urged on the Pāṇḍavas, ever eager though they already were.

sanskrit: kurvantaḥ śāsanaṃ tasya pāṇḍaveyā yaśasvinaḥ saro haṃsā ivāpetur ghnanto droṇarathaṃ prati
english: Obeying his command, the glorious Pāṇḍava warriors swept down upon Droṇa's chariot, slaying as they came, like wild geese descending upon a lake.

sanskrit: gṛhṇītādravatānyonyaṃ vibhītā vinikṛntata ity āsīt tumulaḥ śabdo durdharṣasya rathaṃ prati
english: "Seize them! Charge them! Cut them down without fear!"—such was the tumultuous din that rose about the chariot of the indomitable one.

sanskrit: tato droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇo drauṇī rājā jayadrathaḥ vindānuvindāv avantyau śalyaś cainān avārayan
english: Then Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Droṇa's son, the king, Jayadratha, the two Avanti princes Vinda and Anuvinda, and Śalya held them back.

sanskrit: te tv āryadharmasaṃrabdhā durnivāryā durāsadāḥ śarārtā na juhur droṇaṃ pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: But the Pāñcālas, with the Pāṇḍavas—fired by the duty of the noble, irresistible, hard to assail—though sore wounded by arrows, would not abandon their assault on Droṇa.

sanskrit: tato droṇo 'bhisaṃkruddho visṛjañ śataśaḥ śarān cedipāñcālapāṇḍūnām akarot kadanaṃ mahat
english: Then Droṇa, transported with fury, loosing arrows by the hundred, wrought a great slaughter among the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasya jyātalanirghoṣaḥ śuśruve dikṣu māriṣa vajrasaṃghātasaṃkāśas trāsayan pāṇḍavān bahūn
english: The din of his bowstring and palm-guard, O lord, was heard in every quarter, like the crash of a thunderbolt, terrifying many of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: etasminn antare jiṣṇur hatvā saṃśaptakān balī abyayāt tatra yatra sma droṇaḥ pāṇḍūn pramardati
english: In that interval the mighty Jiṣṇu, having slain the Saṃśaptakas, hastened to the place where Droṇa was crushing the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: taṃ śaraughamahāvartaṃ śoṇitodaṃ mahāhradam tīrṇaḥ saṃśaptakān hatvā pratyadṛśyata phalgunaḥ
english: Having crossed that great lake whose whirlpools were floods of arrows and whose waters were blood, and having slain the Saṃśaptakas, Phalguna came into view.

sanskrit: tasya kīrtimato lakṣma sūryapratimatejasaḥ dīpyamānam apaśyāma tejasā vānaradhvajam
english: We beheld the emblem of that glorious one, splendid as the sun—his ape-bannered standard blazing with radiance.

sanskrit: saṃśaptakasamudraṃ tam ucchoṣyāstragabhastibhiḥ sa pāṇḍavayugāntārkaḥ kurūn apy abhyatītapat
english: Having dried up that ocean of the Saṃśaptakas with the beams of his weapons, that Pāṇḍava—a sun of the world's ending—scorched the Kurus as well.

sanskrit: pradadāha kurūn sarvān arjunaḥ śastratejasā yugānte sarvabhūtāni dhūmaketur ivotthitaḥ
english: Arjuna consumed all the Kurus with the blaze of his weapons, as the fire of doom, risen at the end of the age, consumes all beings.

sanskrit: tena bāṇasahasraughair gajāśvarathayodhinaḥ tāḍyamānāḥ kṣitiṃ jagmur muktaśastrāḥ śarārditāḥ
english: Smitten by him with floods of arrows in their thousands, the warriors on elephants, horses, and chariots, their weapons dropping from their hands and tormented by his shafts, sank to the earth.

sanskrit: ke cid ārtasvaraṃ cakrur vinedur apare punaḥ pārthabāṇahatāḥ ke cin nipetur vigatāsavaḥ
english: Some raised cries of anguish, others shrieked aloud, and some, struck down by Pārtha's arrows, fell lifeless.

sanskrit: teṣām utpatatāṃ kāṃś cit patitāṃś ca parāṅmukhān na jaghānārjuno yodhān yodhavratam anusmaran
english: Mindful of a warrior's vow, Arjuna did not slay those among them who fled, or who had fallen, or who turned their backs.

sanskrit: te viśīrṇarathāśvebhāḥ prāyaśaś ca parāṅmukhāḥ kuravaḥ karṇa karṇeti hā heti ca vicukruśuḥ
english: Their chariots, horses, and elephants shattered, the Kurus, mostly turned to flight, cried out "Karṇa! Karṇa!" and "Alas! Alas!"

sanskrit: tam ādhirathir ākrandaṃ vijñāya śaraṇaiṣiṇām mā bhaiṣṭeti pratiśrutya yayāv abhimukho 'rjunam
english: Hearing that cry of the men who sought refuge, the son of Adhiratha answered, "Fear not!", and advanced to meet Arjuna face to face.

sanskrit: sa bhāratarathaśreṣṭhaḥ sarvabhārataharṣaṇaḥ prāduścakre tad āgneyam astram astravidāṃ varaḥ
english: That best of Bhārata car-warriors, the delight of all the Bhāratas, foremost of those who knew weapons, brought forth the fiery weapon of Agni.

sanskrit: tasya dīptaśaraughasya dīptacāpadharasya ca śaraughāñ śarajālena vidudhāva dhanaṃjayaḥ astram astreṇa saṃvārya prāṇadad visṛjañ śarān
english: Against him, blazing with floods of arrows and wielding a flaming bow, Dhanaṃjaya scattered those streams of shafts with a net of his own; and warding off weapon with weapon, he roared aloud as he loosed his arrows.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca bhīmaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ vivyadhuḥ karṇam āsādya tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Bhīma and the great car-warrior Sātyaki closed upon Karṇa and pierced him, each with three straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: arjunāstraṃ tu rādheyaḥ saṃvārya śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ cāpāni ciccheda viśikhais tribhiḥ
english: But the son of Rādhā, warding off Arjuna's weapon with showers of arrows, cut asunder the bows of those three with three keen shafts.

sanskrit: te nikṛttāyudhāḥ śūrā nirviṣā bhujagā iva rathaśaktīḥ samutkṣipya bhṛśaṃ siṃhā ivānadan
english: Their weapons cut away, those heroes—like serpents drained of venom—snatched up the lances of their chariots and roared aloud like lions.

sanskrit: tā bhujāgrair mahāvegā visṛṣṭā bhujagopamāḥ dīpyamānā mahāśaktyo jagmur ādhirathiṃ prati
english: Hurled with great force from the tips of their arms, those mighty lances, blazing and serpent-like, sped toward the son of Adhiratha.

sanskrit: tā nikṛtya śitair bāṇais tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ nanāda balavān karṇaḥ pārthāya visṛjañ śarān
english: Cutting them down, each with three sharp straight-flying arrows, the mighty Karṇa roared and loosed his shafts at Pārtha.

sanskrit: arjunaś cāpi rādheyaṃ viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ karṇād avarajaṃ bāṇair jaghāna niśitais tribhiḥ
english: And Arjuna too, having pierced the son of Rādhā with seven swift shafts, slew Karṇa's younger brother with three whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatruṃjayaṃ hatvā pārthaḥ ṣaḍbhir ajihmagaiḥ jahāra sadyo bhallena vipāṭasya śiro rathāt
english: Then, having slain Śatruṃjaya with six straight shafts, Pārtha straightway swept the head of Vipāṭa from his chariot with a broad-headed arrow.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām ekenaiva kirīṭinā pramukhe sūtaputrasya sodaryā nihatās trayaḥ
english: Before the very eyes of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons, and in the presence of the charioteer's son, the Diademed One alone slew three brothers.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaḥ samutpatya svarathād vainateyavat varāsinā karṇapakṣāñ jaghāna daśa pañca ca
english: Then Bhīma, springing from his own chariot like the son of Vinatā, slew fifteen of Karṇa's followers with his excellent sword.

sanskrit: punaḥ svaratham āsthāya dhanur ādāya cāparam vivyādha daśabhiḥ karṇaṃ sūtam aśvāṃś ca pañcabhiḥ
english: Mounting his chariot again and taking up another bow, he pierced Karṇa with ten arrows, and his charioteer and horses with five.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumno 'py asivaraṃ carma cādāya bhāsvaram jaghāna candravarmāṇaṃ bṛhatkṣatraṃ ca pauravam
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, taking up an excellent sword and a gleaming shield, slew Candravarman and Bṛhatkṣatra of the Paurava line.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaratham āsthāya pāñcālyo 'nyac ca kārmukam ādāya karṇaṃ vivyādha trisaptatyā nadan raṇe
english: Then mounting his chariot and taking up another bow, the Pāñcāla prince pierced Karṇa with seventy-three arrows, roaring in the battle.

sanskrit: śaineyo 'py anyad ādāya dhanur indrāyudhadyuti sūtaputraṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā viddhvā siṃha ivānadat
english: The grandson of Śini too, taking up another bow that shone like Indra's rainbow, pierced the charioteer's son with sixty-four shafts and roared like a lion.

sanskrit: bhallabhyāṃ sādhumuktābhyāṃ chittvā karṇasya kārmukam punaḥ karṇaṃ tribhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: With two well-aimed broad-headed shafts he cut Karṇa's bow asunder, and again drove three arrows into Karṇa's arms and breast.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano droṇo rājā caiva jayadrathaḥ nimajjamānaṃ rādheyam ujjahruḥ sātyakārṇavāt
english: Then Duryodhana and Droṇa, and King Jayadratha as well, drew up the son of Rādhā, who was sinking, from the ocean that was Sātyaki.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca bhīmaś ca saubhadro 'rjuna eva ca nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sātyakiṃ jugupū raṇe
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Bhīma, Subhadrā's son and Arjuna himself, Nakula and Sahadeva, guarded Sātyaki in the battle.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahāraudraḥ kṣayārthaṃ sarvadhanvinām tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca tyaktvā prāṇān abhūd raṇaḥ
english: Thus did this most fearful battle rage on, for the destruction of all the bowmen—of your men and of the foe alike—who flung their very lives away.

sanskrit: padātirathanāgāśvair gajāśvarathapattayaḥ rathino nāgapattyaśvai rathapattī rathadvipaiḥ
english: With footmen, chariots, elephants, and horses—elephants, horses, chariots, and footmen; car-warriors with elephants, footmen, and horses; chariots and footmen with chariots and elephants—

sanskrit: aśvair aśvā gajair nāgā rathino rathibhiḥ saha saṃsaktāḥ samadṛśyanta pattayaś cāpi pattibhiḥ
english: horse locked with horse, elephant with elephant, car-warrior with car-warrior, and footman with footman, all were seen grappling together.

sanskrit: evaṃ sukalilaṃ yuddham āsīt kravyādaharṣaṇam mahadbhis tair abhītānāṃ yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: So tangled and terrible was that battle, a joy to the eaters of flesh, swelling the realm of Yama with those great and fearless warriors.

sanskrit: tato hatā nararathavājikuñjarair; anekaśo dviparathavājipattayaḥ gajair gajā rathibhir udāyudhā rathā; hayair hayāḥ pattigaṇaiś ca pattayaḥ
english: Then by men, chariots, horses, and elephants were slain, again and again, elephants and chariots, horses and footmen; elephants by elephants, chariots with raised weapons by car-warriors, horses by horses, and footmen by bands of footmen.

sanskrit: rathair dvipā dviradavarair mahāhayā; hayair narā vararathibhiś ca vājinaḥ nirastajihvādaśanekṣaṇāḥ kṣitau; kṣayaṃ gatāḥ pramathitavarmabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: By chariots fell elephants, by lordly elephants the great horses, by horses men, and by mighty car-warriors the steeds—their tongues, teeth, and eyes torn out, their armour and ornaments crushed, they met their end upon the earth.

sanskrit: tathā parair bahukaraṇair varāyudhair; hatā gatāḥ pratibhayadarśanāḥ kṣitim vipothitā hayagajapādatāḍitā; bhṛśākulā rathakhuranemibhir hatāḥ
english: So too were they slain by the foe with many devices and excellent weapons, and sank to the earth, dreadful to behold—mangled, beaten down by the feet of horses and elephants, and crushed in their distress by chariot-wheels and rims and hooves.

sanskrit: pramodane śvāpadapakṣirakṣasāṃ; janakṣaye vartati tatra dāruṇe mahābalās te kupitāḥ parasparaṃ; niṣūdayantaḥ pravicerur ojasā
english: While that terrible destruction of men went on, to the delight of beasts and birds and demons, those mighty warriors, enraged, ranged about with all their force, slaughtering one another.

sanskrit: tato bale bhṛśalulite parasparaṃ; nirīkṣamāṇe rudhiraughasaṃplute divākare 'staṃgirim āsthite śanair; ubhe prayāte śibirāya bhārata
english: Then, when both armies were sorely shattered and drenched in floods of blood, gazing upon one another, and the sun had slowly settled upon the western mountain, both withdrew to their camps, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pūrvam asmāsu bhagneṣu phalgunenāmitaujasā droṇe ca moghasaṃkalpe rakṣite ca yudhiṣṭhire
english: Saṃjaya said: When we had first been broken by Phalguna of boundless might, and Droṇa's purpose had come to nothing and Yudhiṣṭhira had been kept safe,

sanskrit: sarve vidhvastakavacās tāvakā yudhi nirjitāḥ rajasvalā bhṛśodvignā vīkṣamāṇā diśo daśa
english: all your men, their armour shattered, vanquished in the fight, covered with dust and sorely troubled, stood gazing about them in all ten directions.

sanskrit: avahāraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā bhāradvājasya saṃmate labdhalakṣyaiḥ parair dīnā bhṛśāvahasitā raṇe
english: Then, having drawn back with the consent of Bharadvāja's son, they were dejected, while the foe had gained their aim, and they were bitterly mocked in the battle.

sanskrit: ślāghamāneṣu bhūteṣu phalgunasyāmitān guṇān keśavasya ca sauhārde kīrtyamāne 'rjunaṃ prati abhiśastā ivābhūvan dhyānamūkatvam āsthitāḥ
english: And as all beings extolled the boundless virtues of Phalguna, and the loving friendship of Keśava toward Arjuna was praised aloud, your men became as though accursed, and sank into a brooding silence.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye droṇaṃ duryodhano 'bravīt praṇayād abhimānāc ca dviṣadvṛddhyā ca durmanāḥ śṛṇvatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃrabdho vākyakovidaḥ
english: Then, at the hour of dawn, Duryodhana spoke to Droṇa—out of affection, out of wounded pride, and out of grief at the growing power of the foe—heavy at heart, and skilled in speech he spoke in his fury, while all who stood there listened:

sanskrit: nūnaṃ vayaṃ vadhyapakṣe bhavato brahmavittama tathā hi nāgrahīḥ prāptaṃ samīpe 'dya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "Surely we belong to the side you would see slain, O best of those who know the sacred lore; for today you did not seize Yudhiṣṭhira, though he came within your reach.

sanskrit: icchatas te na mucyeta cakṣuḥprāpto raṇe ripuḥ jighṛkṣato rakṣyamāṇaḥ sāmarair api pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: Had you but wished it, no foe once come within your sight in battle could have escaped you, were you minded to seize him—though guarded by the Pāṇḍavas with the very gods themselves.

sanskrit: varaṃ dattvā mama prītaḥ paścād vikṛtavān asi āśābhaṅgaṃ na kurvanti bhaktasyāryāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Having granted me a boon in your favour, you afterward turned against it. The noble never in any way break the hopes of one who is devoted to them."

sanskrit: tato 'prītas tathoktaḥ sa bhāradvājo 'bravīn nṛpam nārhase mānyathā jñātuṃ ghaṭamānaṃ tava priye
english: Then, thus addressed and displeased, the son of Bharadvāja answered the king: "You ought not to think otherwise of me, who strive for your welfare.
